channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: DECODED: THE AI CONVERSATIONS
channel.desc: AI is no longer a technology of the future; it is a current reality reshaping our daily lives and entire industries. Korea, in particular, is one of the countries most dynamically experiencing this change, as AI deeply penetrates various sectors, including aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, and manufacturing. Through [Decoded: The AI Conversations], we will examine where this technology is heading and how it is changing our lives and society, together with leaders guiding the Korean AI industry. This journey features Dr. Kang Sung-ju, also known as the science communicator \"Hang sung\", as a fixed panelist. In the conversation among the MC, the panelist, and the guests, complex AI concepts are naturally \"decoded\" into everyday language. This will be a platform that vividly delivers the frontline of AI innovation where technology, industry, and policy intersect.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

channel.title: DIPLOMAT'S ARCHIVE: HIDDEN STORIES
channel.desc: As of April 2025, S. Korea has established diplomatic relations with a total of 194 countries. Among them are countries that have had ties and exchanges with Korea for hundreds of years. With such long-standing relationships with so many nations, might there be fascinating hidden stories between Korea and the rest of the world that we don?t know yet? \"Diplomat?s Archives: Hidden Stories\" begins with this very question. Together with foreign embassies in Korea, the series uncovers and sheds light on meaningful yet lesser-known stories between Korea and other countries. Through this, we aim to reaffirm the deep friendships that have been built over time, highlight how countries are interconnected?bilaterally and multilaterally? and emphasize the importance of cooperation on the global stage today.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: DECODED: THE AI CONVERSATIONS
channel.desc: AI is no longer a technology of the future; it is a current reality reshaping our daily lives and entire industries. Korea, in particular, is one of the countries most dynamically experiencing this change, as AI deeply penetrates various sectors, including aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, and manufacturing. Through [Decoded: The AI Conversations], we will examine where this technology is heading and how it is changing our lives and society, together with leaders guiding the Korean AI industry. channel.desc: This long-running staple of the C-SPAN2 weekend schedule helps expand the channel's programming beyond politics. channel.desc: Eine von Mozarts Musik inspirierte Crossover-Erfahrung: das ?berraschende und originelle "Spirits of Mozart". In diesem Crossover- interpretieren herausragende Pers?nlichkeiten aus Pop, Jazz und Klassik Mozarts Kompositionen in ihrer pers?nlichen musikalischen Sprache f?r ein breites Publikum des 21. Jahrhunderts. Diese Darbietungen zeigen, dass der Einfluss von Mozarts Musik weit ?ber die Grenzen klassischer Musik hinausreicht. Interpreten wie Dee Dee Bridgewater, der junge Geiger Benjamin Schmid mit Jazz-Band und Orchester, Jethro Tulls S?nger und Fl?tist Ian Anderson und viele andere pr?sentieren Mozart-Arrangements in einer mitrei?enden, elektrisierenden Mischung aus Klassik, Jazz und Popkultur. channel.desc: Das Europakonzert fand 2007 anl?sslich des 125. Jubili?ums in der Heimat der Berliner Philharmoniker, der Hauptstadt Deutschlands statt. Unter dem Motto "Das Jahr 1882" interpretiert das gefeierte Orchester unter der Leitung von Dirigent Sir Simon Rattle Brahms' " f?r Violine, Cello und Orchester", sowie dessen 4. Sinfonie und Wagners "Prel?de des Ersten Aktes" aus Parsifal. Letzteres war 1913 unter der Leitung von Dirigent Alfred Hertz Teil der ersten professionellen Tonaufnahme des Orchesters. Die Solisten der Performance, Lisa Batiashvili (Violine) und Truls M?rk (Cello) sind gleicherma?en junge und gefeierte Virtuosen, die heute regelm??ig in Begleitung der besten Orchester Weltweit auftreten. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Brahms ? Sinfonie Nr. 2 in D-Dur, op. 73
channel.desc: Les Dissonances ist ein K?nstlerkollektiv, das 2004 vom Geiger David Grimal gegr?ndet wurde. Das Ensemble ohne Dirigenten besteht aus Musikern der renommiertesten europ?ischen Orchester, internationalen Solisten und jungen Talenten. In dieser Auff?hrung pr?sentiert Les Dissonances Johannes Brahms' Symphonie Nr. 2 in D-Dur, Op. 73. W?hrend der Komponist viele Jahre ben?tigte, um seine erste Symphonie zu vollenden, schrieb er seine Symphonie Nr. 2 in nur wenigen Monaten, im Sommer 1877 im ruhigen ?sterreichischen Dorf P?rtschach. Das Werk wird oft als seine "Pastorale" bezeichnet und gilt als die sonnigste und optimistischste seiner vier Symphonien. Das Werk ist von lyrischem Charakter und zeichnet sich durch fr?hliche Melodien aus. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2015 in der Philharmonie de Paris, Frankreich, aufgezeichnet.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Die Stimme der Geige
channel.desc: Wie l?sst sich die intime Verbindung eines K?nstlers und seines Instrumentes beschreiben? Der weltbekannte Violinist Frank Peter Zimmerman bezeichnet seine 1711 Stradivarius "Lady Inchiquin" als die "Liebe seines Lebens". Doch wie erlangt ein ehemaliges St?ck Holz solch unsch?tzbaren Wert? Nachdem er das geliebtes Instrument, das der West LB-Bank geh?rte, zur?ckkgeben musste, wendete sich Zimmerman an Martin Schleske, einen Violinmacher, der von Vielen als der "Stradivari des 21. Jahrhunderts" bezeichnet wird. Geschichte der Trennung und Wiedervereinigung des weltweit gefeierten Violinisten Frank Peter Zimmermans und seiner geliebten 1711 Stradivarius ist eng verwoben mit der Suche eines anderen Meisters nach Perfektion: Meister-Violinmacher Martin Schleske bietet Einblicke hinter die Kulissen seiner Arbeit. Dieser Dokumentarfilm befasst sich mit der Reise eines filigranen Instrumentes, von der Werkstatt bis in den saal. Mit dabei: Martin Schleske (Violinmacher).

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: In diesem wunderbaren aus der Kirche der schweizer Stadt Verbier vereinen der griechische Violinspieler Leonidas Kavakos und die chinesische Pianistin Yuja Wang ihre musikalischen Kr?fte in einer Interpretation dreier Sonaten von Johannes Brahms. Leonidas Kavakos wurde 1985 durch seine Teilnahme und Erstplatzierung beim prestigevollen International Jean Sibelius Violin-Wettebwerb bekannt. Gemeinsam mit Yuja Wang, die selbst im jungen Alter bereits eine erfahrene Musikerin ist, schafft er ein eindrucksvolles der Kammermusik. Teil des Programmes sind Brahms 1. Sonate f?r Klavier und Geige, in G-Dur, Op. 78, auch die "Regensonate" genannt, 2. Sonate f?r Klavier und Geige in A-Moll, Op. 100, die"Thuner Sonate", die ein musikalisches Portr?t des schweizerischen Thunersee malt. Das endet mit einem feurigen Abschluss: Brahms 3. Sonate f?r Klavier und Geige in d-Dur, Op. 108. Mit dabei: Leonidas Kavakos (Violine) Yuja Wang (Klavier).

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Beethoven ? Sinfonie Nr. 5 in c-Moll: op. 67
channel.desc: Les Dissonances ist ein K?nstlerkollektiv, das 2004 vom Geiger David Grimal gegr?ndet wurde. Das Ensemble ohne Dirigent besteht aus Musikern der renommiertesten europ?ischen Orchester, internationalen Solisten und jungen Talenten. In dieser Auff?hrung f?hrt Les Dissonances Ludwig van Beethovens Sinfonie Nr. 5 in c-Moll, Op. 67 auf. Beethoven komponierte die Sinfonie Nr. 5 zwischen 1804 und 1808 und vollendete das Werk fast zeitgleich mit seiner Sinfonie Nr. 6, der 'Pastorale'. Beide Sinfonien wurden am 22. Dezember 1808 uraufgef?hrt und waren Teil eines Programms, das ausschlie?lich aus Beethoven-Werken bestand. Die Sinfonie ist eine der bekanntesten Kompositionen der klassischen Musik. Sie beginnt mit dem ber?hmten viert?nigen Motiv, das oft als musikalische Manifestation des 'Schicksals, das an die T?r klopft', interpretiert wird. Diese rhythmische Figur kehrt in verschiedenen Formen in den anderen drei S?tzen der Sinfonie zur?ck. Der zweite Satz besteht aus einer Reihe von lyrischen Variationen ?ber zwei Themen. Der dritte Satz beginnt sanft, f?hrt aber zu einer kraftvollen Hornsektion, die ein Thema pr?sentiert, das das rhythmische Muster des viert?nigen Motivs beinhaltet. Der Satz f?hrt ohne Unterbrechung zum vierten Satz, der mit einem triumphalen Finale in C-Dur endet. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2015 in der Philharmonie de Paris, Frankreich, aufgezeichnet. Mit dabei: David Grimal (Violine).

channel.name: Classica DE

Prosseda bringt das mit einer Interpretation des technisch anspruchsvollen Ballade No. 4, Op. 52 von Chopin zu einem kr?nenden Abschluss. Er ist besonders f?r seine Interpretationen einiger k?rzlich entdeckter Werke von Mendelssohn und seine 9-teilige CD-Serie ?ber Klavierwerke des Komponisten bekannt. Seit 2012 gibt der Italiener zudem Lehrkonzerte mit dem klavierspielenden Roboter TeoTronico. Sein Ziel ist es dabei, den Unterschied zwischen der direkten Umsetzung des Roboters und der menschlichen Interpretationskunst zu verdeutlichen. Mit dabei: Roberto Prosseda (Klavier).

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Dvo??k ? Othello ? Concert Overture, Op. 93
channel.desc: Andris Nelsons pr?sentiert gemeinsam mit seiner damaligen Frau, der gro?en Sopranistin Kristine Opolais, und dem Gewandhausorchester Leipzig ein Antonin Dvo??k gewidmetes Programm. Opolais sing die Melodien, die der Komponist in allen Schichten seiner Musik versteckt hat, mit zarten, warmen und weichen Klangfarben. Nelsons' Tempi bleiben ruhig und entspannt, so dass sich die allgegenw?rtige Sch?nheit von Dvo??ks Musik entfalten und das Gewandhaus in seiner G?nze durchfluten kann. Das Programm beginnt mit Othello, einer ouvert?re f?r Orchester, Op. 93. Opolais interpretiert das "Lied an den Mond" aus Rusalka und "Lieder, die mir meine Mutter beigebracht hat" aus Zigeunerlieder, Op. 55/4. Es folgen die Polonaise und "O, marno, marno to je" aus Rusalka und "Dobr?! J? mu je d?m!... Jak je mi?" aus der Oper Dalibor von Smetana. Das schlie?t mit einer Auff?hrung von Dvo??ks Symphonie Nr. 9 in e-Moll, Op. 95 ("Aus der Neuen Welt"). Aufgezeichnet im Gewandhaus zu Leipzig im Mai 2017. Mit dabei: Kristine Opolais (Sopran).

"Sie h?ren besser, wenn Sie Ihren Kopf unter diese Maschine halten, nicht wahr?", fragte Andr? Stein einst Beethoven. "Inside the Hearing Machine" l?dt uns auf den multisensorischen Spielplatz eines geh?rlosen Komponisten ein, f?r den die Maschine mehr als ein H?rger?t war und der ?ber viel mehr als nur Klang mit seinem Instrument interagierte. channel.desc: This Sonata for Violin and Harpsichord No.6 BWV 1019 is the last of the set of sonatas that Johann Sebastian Bach composed before 1725, probably while working as chapel master in K?then. He presumably wrote these sonatas for Prince Leopold and later adapted them for further use in Leipzig. The different pieces are meant to be a set, just like the Brandenburg concertos, but this last sonata is different from the others in that it has five sections instead of four. channel.desc: Das renommierte franz?sische Streichquartett Quatuor ?b?ne feierte den 250. channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Nachdem er alle 32 Klaviersonaten von Ludwig van Beethoven aufgenommen hatte, um den 250. F?nfzehn Jahre sp?ter, im Jahr 1852, ver?ffentlichte Schumann eine ?berarbeitete Ausgabe des Werkes, in der er zwei Et?den entfernte und einige ?nderungen an der Klavierschrift vornahm. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Beethoven ? Piano Sonata No. 31, Op. 110
channel.desc: Kann es uns gelingen, uns in Beethovens kreativen Geist hineinzuversetzen, besonders in der letzten Phase seines Lebens, als er mit schwerem H?rverlust zu k?mpfen hatte? Tom Beghins neue Aufnahme von Beethovens Klaviersonaten Opus 109, 110 und 111 ist eine k?nstlerische Untersuchung dessen, inwiefern Beethovens Musik durch sein direktes Umfeld gepr?gt wurde, das er sich gemeinsam mit der Hilfe von Kollegen und Freunden schuf. Der Pianist Tom Beghin interpretiert hier nicht nur Beethovens Trilogie pianistischer Meisterwerke auf einem gro?artigen neuen Replikat Beethovens Broadwood-Klavieres, sondern verwendet dabei auch eine Rekonstruktion der Geh?rmaschine, die auf dem Klavier des Komponisten montiert war, damit er weiterhin Musik komponieren und spielen konnte, trotz des schwindenden Geh?rsinns. "Sie h?ren besser, wenn Sie Ihren Kopf unter diese Maschine halten, nicht wahr?", fragte Andr? Stein einst Beethoven. Zwei Jahrhunderte sp?ter k?nnen auch wir unsere K?pfe unter die Maschine halten und uns fragen: H?ren wir Beethoven anders? Beghin zieht uns in das H?rger?t hinein, wo wir die Essenz von Beethovens wilden und unwiderstehlich poetischen musikalischen Eingebungen f?hlen und h?ren. "Inside the Hearing Machine" l?dt uns auf den multisensorischen Spielplatz eines geh?rlosen Komponisten ein, f?r den die Maschine mehr als ein H?rger?t war und der ?ber viel mehr als nur Klang mit seinem Instrument interagierte. Mit dabei: Tom Beghin.

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Tschaikowskis Der Nussknacker ist eines der bekanntesten und beliebtesten St?cke des Komponisten. Die Musik inspirierte viele Choreographen dazu, die bunte Weihnachtsgeschichte von E.T.A. Hoffmann und Alexandre Dumas Senior mithilfe der Sprache des Tanzes zu erz?hlen. Ben Stevenson gilt bis heute als einer der pr?gendsten Figuren in der Geschichte der amerikanischen kunst. Fast 30 Jahre lang war er K?nstlerischer Leiter des Houston Ballet. Unter seiner ?gide erreichte die truppe internationale Bekanntheit. Seit 2003 ist Stevenson nun K?nstlerischer Leiter des Texas Ballet. Seine Produktionen gewannen viele renommierte Preise, wurden von Kritikern gefeiert und in der Op?ra de Paris, dem Canadian National Ballet, La Scala, der Bayerischen Staatsoper, dem London City Ballet und auf vielen weiteren B?hnen aufgef?hrt. Diese Auff?hrung des Nussknackers wurde 2012 im Teatro La Fenice (Venedig) aufgezeichnet. Es tanzt das Estnische Nationalballett mit den Start?nzern Vladislav Lantranov und Galina Laush.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Bach: Goldberg-Variationen BWV 988
channel.desc: Zhu Xiao-Mei interpretiert die Goldberg-Variationen (BWV 988) von J. S. Bach beim Bachfest Leipzig 2014. Das wurde im Juni 2014 in der Thomaskirche aufgezeichnet, wo Bach die meiste Zeit seiner Karriere als Thomaskantor, beziehungsweise musikalischer Leiter des Thomanerchores, verbrachte. Die Goldberg-Variationen bestehen aus einer Arie und einem Satz von 30 Variationen. Das Werk wurde erstmals 1741 ver?ffentlicht und ist nach Johann Gottlieb Goldberg benannt. Im Gegensatz zu anderen melodischen Variationen ?ber ein Thema folgen die Goldberg-Variationen nicht der Melodie, sondern orientieren sich an der Basslinie und Akkordfolge der Arie. Jede dritte Variation der 30-teiligen Reihe ist ein Kanon, der einem aufsteigenden Muster folgt. Die Goldberg-Variationen geh?ren zu den ber?hmtesten Werken Bachs und erlangten ein gr??eres Publikum dank Glenn Goulds legend?ren Aufnahmen des Werks in den Jahren 1955 und 1981. channel.desc: Der mexikanische Dirigent Carlos Miguel Prieto leitet die Orquesta Sinf?nica de Miner?a in einer Auff?hrung der musikalischen Suite "Der Karneval der Tiere" (Le carnaval des animaux, 1886) von Camille Saint-Sa?ns. Diese Suite besteht aus 14 S?tzen, von denen jeder ein anderes Tier darstellt. Das Werk wurde posthum 1922 ver?ffentlicht, da Saint-Sa?ns bef?rchtete, dass seine tierischen Miniaturen, voller am?santer Scherze, seinem Ruf als ernsthafter Komponist schaden k?nnten. Der Satz "Der Schwan", der f?r Cello und zwei Klaviere komponiert ist, ist der einzige, den Saint-Sa?ns zu seinen Lebzeiten ver?ffentlichen lie?. Dieser ikonische Satz zeichnet sich durch eine wundersch?ne, flie?ende Cellomelodie und eine sanfte Klavierbegleitung aus, die das Bild eines anmutig ?ber das Wasser gleitenden Schwans heraufbeschw?rt. Jeder Satz wird von Prieto eingef?hrt. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2021 im Auditorio Nacional in Mexiko-Stadt aufgenommen. Mit dabei: Carlos Miguel Prieto Orquesta Sinfonica de Miner?a.

channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: IVC 2021
channel.desc: Der Tenor Zhuohan Sun (China, 1993) und die Pianistin Sara Pavlovic (Serbien, 1996) f?hren das "Wanderlied" aus Robert Schumanns Kerner-Liedern, Op. 35, auf; "Der Abend kommt gezogen" aus Alphons Diepenbrocks "Drie ballades", Op. 1; Gabriel Faur?s "Prison", Op. 83, No. 1; "Ganymed" aus Hugo Wolfs "Goethe-Liedern"; Franz Schuberts "Nacht und Tr?ume", D. 827; Zaiyi Lu's "The bridge in my homeland"; "Mit Myrten und Rosen" aus Schumanns "Liederkreis", Op. 24; "C" aus Francis Poulencs "Deux po?mes de Louis Aragon", FP 122; und "Scheiden und Meiden" aus Gustav Mahlers "Liedern und Ges?ngen aus der Jugendzeit". Die Auff?hrungen stammen aus dem Finale der International Vocal Competition 2021 ? Lied Duo. Diese Auff?hrung wurde in der Verkadefabriek in 's-Hertogenbosch, Niederlande, aufgezeichnet. Mit dabei: Zhuohan Sun (Tenor) Sara Pavlovic (Pianistin).[(96057)]

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Magical Japanese
channel.desc: The Japanese language is rich in words and expressions influenced by nature, history and culture. This episode looks at words related to trees. Japan is a land of trees - two-thirds of the country is covered by forests. Trees support people's lives, and in turn, they have a deep respect for trees. Various expressions relating to trees have developed over time. Join poet, literary translator and long-time Japan resident Peter MacMillan and explore unique words and the culture behind them.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: Teams of local residents pour heart and soul into the construction of handmade rockets called ryusei that feature in the Yoshida Ryusei matsuri. The rockets carry local hopes and prayers high in the sky over Chichibu, Saitama Prefecture. Seventeen teams made ryusei rockets for the event in October, 2022, which was the first time the event had been held in three years. Each team has its own black powder recipe with unique ingredients and ratios to make their rocket soar.

channel.title: Little Charo
channel.desc: This program is an animation series about a Japanese dog, Charo. He meets and is helped by many mythical creatures of Northern Japan as he searches for eight star talismans.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Japanology Plus Mini
channel.desc: Once thought to have no dinosaur fossils, Japan is now a hot spot for dinosaur discovery. The excavation of Kamuysaurus japonicus in Hokkaido Prefecture overturned the conventional wisdom. It sparked a nationwide enthusiasm for dinosaurs that led to new forms of entertainment, including dinosaur robots in hotels and mechanical dino-suits used in live performances. We look into Japan's love for dinosaurs.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: A Cat's Eye View Of Japan
channel.desc: Chibita is a friendly cat who lives at a souvenir shop near Chusonji Temple, a World Heritage Site. Popo lives at a horseback riding club with 20 horses! At a rose garden, we meet handsome Kikujiro.

channel.title: Anime Manga Explosion
channel.desc: This episode spotlights next-generation creator Yamashita Shingo, known for his key animation work on NARUTO SHIPPUDEN and opening direction for JUJUTSU KAISEN. Plus, we follow Yamashita behind the scenes as he directs his new feature film, Cosmic Princess Kaguya! See how he blends cutting-edge tools with a fresh creative vision to craft anime.\nThe subtitle \"Oshi no Ko OP (2023)\" at 22'48\" was corrected to \"Oshi no Ko ED (2023)\" on February 2, 2026.

channel.desc: No description available.

channel.title: The New Adventures Of Rockie And Her Friends
channel.desc: Shelly's mother is always busy running her caf?. Shelly tries to get her attention by drawing a picture of her, but when her attempt fails, she runs off from home.\n\nEducational theme: Having love and gratitude for one's family, and having a fulfilling family life.

channel.desc: Inoue Masae makes koji, an essential fermented ingredient in Japanese cuisine. Her methods, and her quaint shop, have barely changed in generations.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Core Kyoto
channel.desc: In clamp resist dyeing, fabric is pressed between 2 boards to create shapes. Perfect shading may result from sections randomly touching in the dye, producing beautiful patterns. Discover the future of tie-dyeing.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Easy Japanese For Work
channel.desc: This episode is about making apologies. Loraine Paz Amoro Oledan-san moved to Japan at the end of 2018 to work at a housekeeping company. Starting next week, she will be responsible for cleaning actual homes. She knows how to carry out her work and has learned the Japanese phrases she will need to use. But you never know what unexpected things may happen! Loraine-san will tackle a roleplay to help her explain properly and apologize. She'll learn from experts what to focus on when she does this in Japan.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Zero Waste Life
channel.desc: Some 20% of grown flowers for sale in Japan are discarded as substandard. Nakanishi Megumi uses them to make candles. Just like the flawed beauty of humanity, waste flowers, too, have a unique charm.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Matsuri: The Heartbeat Of Japan
channel.desc: On New Year's Eve, performers dress as terrifying monsters called namahage. They barge into people's homes, condemning laziness and frightening children. But this good-natured tradition strengthens family and community bonds. In Tayazawa, a small village in Akita Prefecture, the practice came to an end several years ago, but was recently restarted by an enthusiastic group of locals. They made costumes and succeeded in reviving a custom at risk of slipping away.
